core_concepts.statement: A person's income ceiling may be influenced by internal beliefs and tolerance for success.
Learned beliefs about money can influence pricing, selling behavior, and the emotional response to receiving money.
Sales situations can trigger fight, flight, freeze, or other protective nervous-system responses.
Undercharging can sometimes function as protection from rejection, judgment, or perceived social risk rather than simply reflecting modesty.
Excessive over-delivering can sometimes reflect anxious pleasing or an attempt to earn safety and acceptance.

audience_insights.statement: The audience often has substantial expertise but may still hesitate to charge according to the value they provide.
Fear of appearing pushy, greedy, or overly sales-focused can interfere with confident selling.
Physical sensations such as jaw, diaphragm, or general body tension may appear around pricing and sales conversations.

psychological_mechanisms.name: fight_flight_freeze
psychological_mechanisms.description: Protective nervous-system responses that may appear when a person perceives social, financial, or rejection-related threat.

psychological_mechanisms.name: co_regulation
psychological_mechanisms.description: Interpersonal nervous-system regulation and mirroring that may influence how people experience sales conversations.

psychological_mechanisms.name: self_worth_pricing_link
psychological_mechanisms.description: The perceived relationship between self-worth, pricing confidence, and tolerance for rejection.

key_messages.statement: The problem may not be a lack of sales scripts; the underlying issue can be the emotional and physiological response to selling.
Higher pricing does not have to mean more pressure, manipulation, or burnout.
Calm authority can replace anxious over-explaining and over-delivering.

beliefs_to_challenge: My niche is too complex to sell.
To earn more I simply need to work more.
beliefs_to_reinforce: Expertise and self-worth do not require constant over-delivery.
Selling can be calm and ethical.
Pricing can be approached without shame.
Regulating the body can support clearer behavior in stressful sales situations.

unvalidated.statement: Relatable expert behaviors and subtle self-sabotage may create strong engagement because the audience recognizes itself in the behavior.

experimental.pattern: Expose a familiar expert behavior and reveal a less obvious psychological reason behind it.
Challenge a common sales belief by reframing it as a nervous-system or self-worth issue.
